newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico net assets up slightly in week to Oct 18.
newsitem.headline: Mexico net assets up slightly in week to Oct 18.

text.p: Banco de Mexico said Tuesday its net international assets as of October 18, 1996 were $3.908 billion, compared with $3.893 billion on October 11.
The central bank said that its net international reserves as of the same date were $15.739 billion, compared with $15.836 billion on October 11.
It said the increase of $15 million in international assets was due to:
- Revenues from operations with state oil firm Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) worth $269 million
- A net sale of currency to the federal government for $261 million to cover external debt service
- Other foreign exchange revenues worth a net $7 million.

Banco de Mexico said the monetary base rose 896 million pesos in the same period. The government bank support fund Fobaproa withdrew 1.21 billion pesos from its account at the central bank to support an unnamed financial institution.
The federal government's deposits at the central bank fell by 4.51 billion pesos due to funds transfers to states and the purchase of foreign exchange for foreign debt service payments.
Central bank credit to financial institutions fell by 3.293 billion pesos to neutralise the impact of the federal government and Fobaproa withdrawals.
The following tables detail Banco de Mexico's assets and net domestic credit. All figures are in billions of pesos, unless otherwise indicated.
*Net International Assets are defined as gross international assets minus central bank liabilities with the IMF and assets of less than a six month duration from other central banks.
